newsitem.title: USA: Baxter operating results higher, expenses cut net income.
newsitem.headline: Baxter operating results higher, expenses cut net income.

text.p: Baxter International Inc. Thursday reported higher second-quarter operating results, but net income fell as the medical products company stepped up spending on research and development, and marketing and administration.
Net income from continuing operations rose 14 percent to $162 million from $142 million in the 1996 period. Operating earnings per share grew 12 percent to 58 cents from 52 cents.
However, the Deerfield, Ill.-based company said its net income fell to $162 million, or 58 cents a share, from $176 million, or 65 cents a share, over the same period.
Marketing and administrative expenses jumped to $347 million from $282 million, while research and development costs rose to $95 million from $84 million.
Sales rose to $1.6 billion from $1.3 billion, led by Baxter's Biotech and IV Systems/Medical Products businesses.

"Our strong second-quarter performance is right on track with our 1997 financial commitments," said Vernon Loucks Jr., Baxter's chairman. "We continue to drive solid growth by successfully executing our strategies of technological innovation and global expansion.
Baxter said it expects to grow its 1997 net income in the "low double digits" and exceed its goal of generating at least $300 million in operational cash flow.
Baxter's stock rose 31.25 cents to $57.8125 on the New York Stock Exchange in midday trading.
